Read /home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/.worktrees/odi-mascot/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-odi-mascot-design.md

Before you answer, skim the actual repository so your questions are grounded in reality (the repo root is /home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/.worktrees/odi-mascot). Report only the questions you'd still need answered before you could plan this well: places where you'd have to guess and a wrong guess would matter. For each, give the question and why the answer changes the plan. Rank them by importance.

Skip anything the document explicitly leaves to the builder, and anything you could reasonably decide yourself. Skip nitpicks about wording.

Deliberately excludes `website/` (see Non-goals). 7: 8: ## Intent 9: 10: The project is public and forkable. Its name, its README, and its UI are all 11: copyable, but a *character* is much harder to copy credibly: it carries taste, 12: history, and a recognizable silhouette that, once people meet it, they expect 13: to see again. Odi is that character — the friendly face of Outcome-Driven 14: Innovation, present in the terminal, in the studio, in the app icon, and in the 15: favicon. 16: 17: Odi is also a defensive asset. A distinctive mascot is a weak trademark: a 18: fork can copy the README, but a fork that ships Odi has visibly copied 19: Agentic ODI, and the provenance story ("the one with the otter") compounds. 20: 21: The mascot must be **cute** (people should smile at it) and **professional** 22: (nobody should be embarrassed to see it in a professional product). It must be 23: **legible at 16 pixels** and **honest at 1024**. 24: 25: ## Goals 26: 27: 1. One character, one silhouette, recognizable at 16 px, on every surface. 28: 2. A construction that is mathematically deliberate — golden-ratio derived 29: proportions — so the character reads as designed rather than doodled. 30: 3. Assets that are **reproducible from source**: a committed generator, not 31: hand-exported binaries, so a fork can see exactly how every pixel was made. 32: 4. Zero new runtime dependencies. The generator uses only what the repo already 33: declares. 34: 5. A brand guide that a third party can follow without asking us. 35: 36: ## Non-goals 37: 38: - **No change to `website/`.** The marketing site is mid-redesign on 39: `feature/gh-pages-redesign`, which rewrites `website/` wholesale. Touching 40: `website/assets/mark.svg` or `favicon.svg` here guarantees a conflict on that 41: branch. The mascot lands in `brand/` and the site swap is a documented 42: two-line follow-up on the redesign branch. 43: - **No new licensing terms.** The repo already ships an MIT `LICENSE` 44: (see `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-repository-structure.md`). The mascot 45: is covered by it. What we add is a *provenance* note, not a legal claim. 46: - **No animation, no sprite sheet, no 3D.** First iteration is static art. 47: - **No mascot in every surface.** A mascot on every pixel is noise. It goes 48: where a human would look for the product's face: the app icon, the favicon, 49: the studio's brand mark, the terminal banner, and the README. 50: - **No emoji.** The repo's own website test suite bans emoji; the CLI already 51: uses a few, but the mascot must not depend on them. 52: 53: ## The character 54: 55: **Name:** Odi. Spelled exactly like the `odi` binary, pronounced "odee". 56: 57: **Species:** otter (sea otter). 58: 59: **Why an otter.** The name is the hook — "Odi the Otter" is alliterative, 60: memorable, and rhymes with the product without impersonating anything. The 61: species carries the semantics: otters are the tool-using problem solvers of 62: the animal world. They take an ambiguous shell, a stone, and a current, and 63: they *engineer* an outcome from it. That is the product thesis in one animal: 64: take messy human context, find the tool that turns it into a measurable 65: customer outcome. Otters are also wide-headed, round-eyed, and warm brown — 66: cute without being saccharine, and visually distinct from every other 67: developer mascot in wide use. 68: 69: **Deliberate exclusions.** No cats (Mistral's Le Chat, and the feline trope is 70: crowded). No octocat (GitHub trademark). No penguin (Tux). No dog (reads as 71: Garfield's Odie). No bee (Honeycomb). An otter is not currently a 72: developer-tool mascot, which is exactly the point: the silhouette is 73: unclaimed. 74: 75: **Personality:** curious, competent, a little bit pleased with itself. Not a 76: robot, not an anthropomorph in a hard hat, not a "smart" creature with a 77: visor. Just a friendly otter who has clearly read the manual. 78: 79: ## Golden-ratio construction 80: 81: Every proportion below is derived from a single constant, φ = 1.6180339887, 82: applied to a **32 × 32 master pixel grid**. The numbers in the table are the 83: literal pixel values the generator uses, so the construction is checkable, not 84: decorative. 85: 86: The construction unit is the head width **W = 20 px**. Every other dimension 87: is W divided by a power of φ, rounded to the nearest whole pixel (φⁿ for 88: n = 1, 2, 3, 4 gives 1.618, 2.618, 4.236, 6.854). 89: 90: | Feature | Rule | Value (px) | Golden point | 91: |---|---|---|---| 92: | Canvas | — | 32 × 32 | — | 93: | Head width `W` | unit | 20 | — | 94: | Head height | `W / φ` | 12 | wide otter skull | 95: | Eye separation (centre-to-centre) | `W / φ` | 12 | eyes at x = 16 ± 6 | 96: | Eye diameter | `W / φ²` | 8 → capped at 4 for legibility | — | 97: | Muzzle width | `W / φ²` | 8 | — | 98: | Muzzle height | `W / φ³` | 5 | — | 99: | Nose width | `W / φ³` | 4 | — | 100: | Ear diameter | `W / φ³` | 4 | — | 101: | Body width | `W / φ` | 12 | shoulders | 102: | Body height | `W / φ²` | 8 | visible bust | 103: | Spark radius | `W / φ⁴` | 2 | the "outcome" apex dot | 104: | Ear span | `W` | 20 | ears at the head's edges | 105: 106: **The two-ladder composition.** Odi is built from two nested golden 107: rectangles: the head (20 × 12, ratio 1.667 ≈ φ) sits inside the bust 108: (20 × 20, a true golden rectangle). The eyes divide the head's width at 109: 1 : 0.618 : 1. The muzzle occupies the golden section of the lower head. The 110: ear tips land on the horizontal golden section of the canvas. Read as a 111: silhouette, the whole character is a golden rectangle; read as a face, the 112: features are at their golden points. 113: 114: **The spark.** The existing site mark is an ascending two-step polyline with 115: an apex dot — a rising opportunity curve. Odi carries that dot: a single 116: accent-coloured spark above the head, sized `W / φ⁴`. It is the one element 117: that ties the character to the product's existing visual language, and it is 118: the character's *signal*: the outcome Odi is looking for. 119: 120: ## Palette 121: 122: The mascot must work on the studio's near-black chrome (`--bg: #0a0b0e`) and 123: on the website's light pages. A warm subject on a cool ground does both. 124: 125: | Token | Hex | Use | 126: |---|---|---| 127: | `odi-ink` | `#1B1410` | outline, nose, pupils | 128: | `odi-fur` | `#B4794C` | main coat | 129: | `odi-fur-light` | `#DCA871` | cheeks, brow, belly edge | 130: | `odi-cream` | `#F6EAD8` | muzzle, chest, eye highlight | 131: | `odi-accent` | `#8B8CF8` | the spark (studio `--accent`) | 132: | `odi-tile` | `#131722` | app-icon tile (matches the site mark tile) | 133: 134: `odi-accent` is the studio's existing accent, so the mascot is already on 135: brand. The coat browns are the only new colours in the system, and they are 136: warm enough to read as "character" against the cool indigo/blue chrome. 137: 138: ## Asset inventory 139: 140: Everything lives under `brand/`, generated by a committed script, and 141: committed to the repo. 142: 143: ```text 144: brand/ 145: README.md # the brand guide (public, standalone) 146: assets/ 147: odi-mascot.svg # full bust, vector, with a φ guide layer 148: odi-head.svg # head-only, vector (icon source) 149: odi-lockup.svg # mascot + "odi" wordmark, vector 150: odi-mascot-256.png # hero raster (README, studio) 151: odi-mascot-512.png 152: odi-mascot-1024.png 153: odi-head-1024.png # icon source raster 154: favicon.ico # 16/32/48/64 multi-size 155: odi-ascii.txt # the terminal banner, plain text 156: src/ 157: odi_mascot.py # the generator: geometry, palette, raster, vector 158: tests/ 159: test_brand_assets.py # asset contract + generator parity 160: tools/ 161: render.py # regenerate everything: `uv run python brand/tools/render.py` 162: ``` 163: 164: **One source of truth.** `brand/src/odi_mascot.py` holds the palette, the φ 165: constants, and the raster geometry. The PNGs, the SVGs, the ICO, and the ASCII 166: banner are all derived from it. `brand/tests/` asserts that the committed 167: binaries match a fresh render, so the art can never silently drift from its 168: source. 169: 170: **Rasterizer.** A tiny shape-and-outline rasterizer, not hand-placed pixels: 171: the generator draws ellipses and rounded rects onto the 32 × 32 grid, then 172: adds a 1 px `odi-ink` outline around the silhouette — the standard pixel-art 173: technique that produces clean, symmetric, professional edges. Features 174: (eyes, nose, muzzle, spark) are stamped on top, and a 1 px `odi-cream` 175: highlight is added to each eye. 176: 177: **The ICO** is written by Pillow (already a root dev dependency) with embedded 178: PNG frames. The **Tauri icon set** (`apps/studio/src-tauri/icons/*`) is 179: regenerated by the already-declared `@tauri-apps/cli` from `odi-head-1024.png`, 180: so `.icns`, `.ico`, and every `Square*Logo.png` stay canonical. 181: 182: **The SVG** is emitted as a true `` per pixel with 183: `shape-rendering="crispEdges"`, so it stays pixel-exact at any size and can 184: carry a toggleable φ guide layer (`data-guides="true"`) that draws the golden 185: rectangles over the art for documentation. 186: 187: ## Surfaces 188: 189: | Surface | Change | File | 190: |---|---|---| 191: | App icon | Replace the purple gradient placeholder with Odi's head on the brand tile | `apps/studio/src-tauri/icons/*` | 192: | Studio favicon | `favicon.svg` + `favicon.ico` + `apple-touch-icon.png` | `apps/studio/public/` | 193: | SPA `` | Replace the dead `/vite.svg` reference | `apps/studio/index.html` | 194: | Studio brand mark | Odi's head replaces the generic `SparkIcon` in the bar's brand slot | `apps/studio/src/components/layout/StudioBar.tsx` | 195: | Studio mascot component | Inline SVG component, size-prop, no dependency | `apps/studio/src/components/OdiMascot.tsx` | 196: | CLI banner | Odi's ASCII bust printed on chat start, truecolor when the terminal supports it | `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/mascot.py`, `chat.py` | 197: | README | Hero image at the top + a short brand pointer | `README.md` | 198: | Brand guide | Palette, φ construction, usage, provenance | `brand/README.md` | 199: 200: **Studio mark slot.** `StudioBar.tsx` already has a `brand__mark` span 201: holding a `SparkIcon`. Odi's head replaces that glyph and the existing 202: `brand__wordmark` text is untouched, so the layout does not move. The mascot 203: component is inline SVG (not an ``) so it inherits the bar's sizing and 204: needs no extra request. 205: 206: **CLI banner.** The banner is a static string constant in 207: `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/mascot.py`, printed at chat start 208: (`chat.py`, alongside the existing "Agentic ODI · interactive" line). It is 209: truecolor ANSI when stdout is a TTY and plain ASCII otherwise, and it honors 210: `NO_COLOR`. The module imports nothing heavy, so the `--version` / `--help` 211: fast path (guarded by `apps/cli/tests/test_startup_perf.py`) is unaffected. 212: 213: **README hero.** A centred `` pointing at `brand/assets/odi-mascot-256.png` 214: under the existing centred title block. 215: 216: ## Originality and provenance 217: 218: The point of a mascot is that it is *ours*. The design doc and the generator 219: are the evidence: 220: 221: - Odi is an original character built from geometric primitives by a committed 222: script. No traced, generated-from-prompt, or third-party art. 223: - The species (otter) is not used as a developer-tool mascot by any widely 224: known product, so there is no crowd to blend into. 225: - The construction is published in `brand/README.md`, including the φ table, so 226: a reviewer can verify the character was designed rather than copied. 227: - The repo's MIT `LICENSE` covers the artwork. The brand guide states the 228: artwork is original work by the project maintainers. 229: 230: **Honest limitation.** A mascot is a weak trademark and no part of this design 231: should be read as a legal opinion. What it does provide is *provenance*: a 232: fork that ships Odi is visibly a fork of Agentic ODI, which is the practical 233: protection the maintainer asked for. 234: 235: ## Accessibility 236: 237: - The mascot is decorative everywhere it appears: `aria-hidden="true"` in the 238: studio, `alt=""` in the README, and never the only label of a control. 239: - The CLI banner is decorative text; it carries no information that is not 240: also in the lines beside it. 241: - Every mascot color clears 3:1 against the surface it sits on. The fur/ink 242: pair clears 7:1. 243: - Nothing about the mascot's meaning is conveyed by color alone; the spark is 244: a shape, not just a hue. 245: 246: ## What's left for the builder 247: 248: 1. Build the generator, get the raster looking cute, iterate. 249: 2. Emit the SVG, ICO, ASCII banner, and the Tauri icon set. 250: 3. Wire the studio, the CLI, and the README. 251: 4. Write `brand/README.md` and the asset tests. 252: 5. Keep CI green: root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` must pass for 253: the new Python, and the new `brand/tests` must pass under the root 254: `uv run pytest` run. # Odi the Otter — mascot and brand identity — design

**Status:** approved for implementation
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Scope:** `brand/` (new, source of truth), `apps/studio` (SPA + Tauri), `apps/cli`,
`README.md`. Deliberately excludes `website/` (see Non-goals).

## Intent

The project is public and forkable. Its name, its README, and its UI are all
copyable, but a *character* is much harder to copy credibly: it carries taste,
history, and a recognizable silhouette that, once people meet it, they expect
to see again. Odi is that character — the friendly face of Outcome-Driven
Innovation, present in the terminal, in the studio, in the app icon, and in the
favicon.

Odi is also a defensive asset. A distinctive mascot is a weak trademark: a
fork can copy the README, but a fork that ships Odi has visibly copied
Agentic ODI, and the provenance story ("the one with the otter") compounds.

Deliberately excludes `website/` (see Non-goals). ## Intent The project is public and forkable. Its name, its README, and its UI are all copyable, but a *character* is much harder to copy credibly: it carries taste, history, and a recognizable silhouette that, once people meet it, they expect to see again. Odi is that character — the friendly face of Outcome-Driven Innovation, present in the terminal, in the studio, in the app icon, and in the favicon. Odi is also a defensive asset. A distinctive mascot is a weak trademark: a fork can copy the README, but a fork that ships Odi has visibly copied Agentic ODI, and the provenance story ("the one with the otter") compounds. The mascot must be **cute** (people should smile at it) and **professional** (nobody should be embarrassed to see it in a professional product). It must be **legible at 16 pixels** and **honest at 1024**. ## Goals 1. One character, one silhouette, recognizable at 16 px, on every surface. 2. A construction that is mathematically deliberate — golden-ratio derived proportions — so the character reads as designed rather than doodled. 3. Assets that are **reproducible from source**: a committed generator, not hand-exported binaries, so a fork can see exactly how every pixel was made. 4. Zero new runtime dependencies. The generator uses only what the repo already declares. 5. A brand guide that a third party can follow without asking us. ## Non-goals - **No change to `website/`.** The marketing site is mid-redesign on `feature/gh-pages-redesign`, which rewrites `website/` wholesale. Touching `website/assets/mark.svg` or `favicon.svg` here guarantees a conflict on that branch. The mascot lands in `brand/` and the site swap is a documented two-line follow-up on the redesign branch. - **No new licensing terms.** The repo already ships an MIT `LICENSE` (see `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-repository-structure.md`). The mascot is covered by it. What we add is a *provenance* note, not a legal claim. - **No animation, no sprite sheet, no 3D.** First iteration is static art. - **No mascot in every surface.** A mascot on every pixel is noise. It goes where a human would look for the product's face: the app icon, the favicon, the studio's brand mark, the terminal banner, and the README. - **No emoji.** The repo's own website test suite bans emoji; the CLI already uses a few, but the mascot must not depend on them. ## The character **Name:** Odi. Spelled exactly like the `odi` binary, pronounced "odee". **Species:** otter (sea otter). **Why an otter.** The name is the hook — "Odi the Otter" is alliterative, memorable, and rhymes with the product without impersonating anything. The species carries the semantics: otters are the tool-using problem solvers of the animal world. They take an ambiguous shell, a stone, and a current, and they *engineer* an outcome from it. That is the product thesis in one animal: take messy human context, find the tool that turns it into a measurable customer outcome. Otters are also wide-headed, round-eyed, and warm brown — cute without being saccharine, and visually distinct from every other developer mascot in wide use. **Deliberate exclusions.** No cats (Mistral's Le Chat, and the feline trope is crowded). No octocat (GitHub trademark). No penguin (Tux). No dog (reads as Garfield's Odie). No bee (Honeycomb). An otter is not currently a developer-tool mascot, which is exactly the point: the silhouette is unclaimed. **Personality:** curious, competent, a little bit pleased with itself. Not a robot, not an anthropomorph in a hard hat, not a "smart" creature with a visor. Just a friendly otter who has clearly read the manual. ## Golden-ratio construction Every proportion below is derived from a single constant, φ = 1.6180339887, applied to a **32 × 32 master pixel grid**. The numbers in the table are the literal pixel values the generator uses, so the construction is checkable, not decorative. The construction unit is the head width **W = 20 px**. Every other dimension is W divided by a power of φ, rounded to the nearest whole pixel (φⁿ for n = 1, 2, 3, 4 gives 1.618, 2.618, 4.236, 6.854). | Feature | Rule | Value (px) | Golden point | |---|---|---|---| | Canvas | — | 32 × 32 | — | | Head width `W` | unit | 20 | — | | Head height | `W / φ` | 12 | wide otter skull | | Eye separation (centre-to-centre) | `W / φ` | 12 | eyes at x = 16 ± 6 | | Eye diameter | `W / φ²` | 8 → capped at 4 for legibility | — | | Muzzle width | `W / φ²` | 8 | — | | Muzzle height | `W / φ³` | 5 | — | | Nose width | `W / φ³` | 4 | — | | Ear diameter | `W / φ³` | 4 | — | | Body width | `W / φ` | 12 | shoulders | | Body height | `W / φ²` | 8 | visible bust | | Spark radius | `W / φ⁴` | 2 | the "outcome" apex dot | | Ear span | `W` | 20 | ears at the head's edges | **The two-ladder composition.** Odi is built from two nested golden rectangles: the head (20 × 12, ratio 1.667 ≈ φ) sits inside the bust (20 × 20, a true golden rectangle). The eyes divide the head's width at 1 : 0.618 : 1. The muzzle occupies the golden section of the lower head. The ear tips land on the horizontal golden section of the canvas. Read as a silhouette, the whole character is a golden rectangle; read as a face, the features are at their golden points. **The spark.** The existing site mark is an ascending two-step polyline with an apex dot — a rising opportunity curve. Odi carries that dot: a single accent-coloured spark above the head, sized `W / φ⁴`. It is the one element that ties the character to the product's existing visual language, and it is the character's *signal*: the outcome Odi is looking for. ## Palette The mascot must work on the studio's near-black chrome (`--bg: #0a0b0e`) and on the website's light pages. A warm subject on a cool ground does both. | Token | Hex | Use | |---|---|---| | `odi-ink` | `#1B1410` | outline, nose, pupils | | `odi-fur` | `#B4794C` | main coat | | `odi-fur-light` | `#DCA871` | cheeks, brow, belly edge | | `odi-cream` | `#F6EAD8` | muzzle, chest, eye highlight | | `odi-accent` | `#8B8CF8` | the spark (studio `--accent`) | | `odi-tile` | `#131722` | app-icon tile (matches the site mark tile) | `odi-accent` is the studio's existing accent, so the mascot is already on brand. The coat browns are the only new colours in the system, and they are warm enough to read as "character" against the cool indigo/blue chrome. ## Asset inventory Everything lives under `brand/`, generated by a committed script, and committed to the repo. ```text brand/ README.md # the brand guide (public, standalone) assets/ odi-mascot.svg # full bust, vector, with a φ guide layer odi-head.svg # head-only, vector (icon source) odi-lockup.svg # mascot + "odi" wordmark, vector odi-mascot-256.png # hero raster (README, studio) odi-mascot-512.png odi-mascot-1024.png odi-head-1024.png # icon source raster favicon.ico # 16/32/48/64 multi-size odi-ascii.txt # the terminal banner, plain text src/ odi_mascot.py # the generator: geometry, palette, raster, vector tests/ test_brand_assets.py # asset contract + generator parity tools/ render.py # regenerate everything: `uv run python brand/tools/render.py` ``` **One source of truth.** `brand/src/odi_mascot.py` holds the palette, the φ constants, and the raster geometry. The PNGs, the SVGs, the ICO, and the ASCII banner are all derived from it. `brand/tests/` asserts that the committed binaries match a fresh render, so the art can never silently drift from its source. **Rasterizer.** A tiny shape-and-outline rasterizer, not hand-placed pixels: the generator draws ellipses and rounded rects onto the 32 × 32 grid, then adds a 1 px `odi-ink` outline around the silhouette — the standard pixel-art technique that produces clean, symmetric, professional edges. Features (eyes, nose, muzzle, spark) are stamped on top, and a 1 px `odi-cream` highlight is added to each eye. **The ICO** is written by Pillow (already a root dev dependency) with embedded PNG frames. The **Tauri icon set** (`apps/studio/src-tauri/icons/*`) is regenerated by the already-declared `@tauri-apps/cli` from `odi-head-1024.png`, so `.icns`, `.ico`, and every `Square*Logo.png` stay canonical. **The SVG** is emitted as a true `` per pixel with `shape-rendering="crispEdges"`, so it stays pixel-exact at any size and can carry a toggleable φ guide layer (`data-guides="true"`) that draws the golden rectangles over the art for documentation. ## Surfaces | Surface | Change | File | |---|---|---| | App icon | Replace the purple gradient placeholder with Odi's head on the brand tile | `apps/studio/src-tauri/icons/*` | | Studio favicon | `favicon.svg` + `favicon.ico` + `apple-touch-icon.png` | `apps/studio/public/` | | SPA `` | Replace the dead `/vite.svg` reference | `apps/studio/index.html` | | Studio brand mark | Odi's head replaces the generic `SparkIcon` in the bar's brand slot | `apps/studio/src/components/layout/StudioBar.tsx` | | Studio mascot component | Inline SVG component, size-prop, no dependency | `apps/studio/src/components/OdiMascot.tsx` | | CLI banner | Odi's ASCII bust printed on chat start, truecolor when the terminal supports it | `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/mascot.py`, `chat.py` | | README | Hero image at the top + a short brand pointer | `README.md` | | Brand guide | Palette, φ construction, usage, provenance | `brand/README.md` | **Studio mark slot.** `StudioBar.tsx` already has a `brand__mark` span holding a `SparkIcon`. Odi's head replaces that glyph and the existing `brand__wordmark` text is untouched, so the layout does not move. The mascot component is inline SVG (not an ``) so it inherits the bar's sizing and needs no extra request. **CLI banner.** The banner is a static string constant in `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/mascot.py`, printed at chat start (`chat.py`, alongside the existing "Agentic ODI · interactive" line). It is truecolor ANSI when stdout is a TTY and plain ASCII otherwise, and it honors `NO_COLOR`. The module imports nothing heavy, so the `--version` / `--help` fast path (guarded by `apps/cli/tests/test_startup_perf.py`) is unaffected. **README hero.** A centred `` pointing at `brand/assets/odi-mascot-256.png` under the existing centred title block. ## Originality and provenance The point of a mascot is that it is *ours*. The design doc and the generator are the evidence: - Odi is an original character built from geometric primitives by a committed script. No traced, generated-from-prompt, or third-party art. - The species (otter) is not used as a developer-tool mascot by any widely known product, so there is no crowd to blend into. - The construction is published in `brand/README.md`, including the φ table, so a reviewer can verify the character was designed rather than copied. - The repo's MIT `LICENSE` covers the artwork. The brand guide states the artwork is original work by the project maintainers. **Honest limitation.** A mascot is a weak trademark and no part of this design should be read as a legal opinion. What it does provide is *provenance*: a fork that ships Odi is visibly a fork of Agentic ODI, which is the practical protection the maintainer asked for. ## Accessibility - The mascot is decorative everywhere it appears: `aria-hidden="true"` in the studio, `alt=""` in the README, and never the only label of a control. - The CLI banner is decorative text; it carries no information that is not also in the lines beside it. - Every mascot color clears 3:1 against the surface it sits on. The fur/ink pair clears 7:1. - Nothing about the mascot's meaning is conveyed by color alone; the spark is a shape, not just a hue. ## What's left for the builder 1. Build the generator, get the raster looking cute, iterate. 2. Emit the SVG, ICO, ASCII banner, and the Tauri icon set. 3. Wire the studio, the CLI, and the README. 4. Write `brand/README.md` and the asset tests. 5. Keep CI green: root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` must pass for the new Python, and the new `brand/tests` must pass under the root `uv run pytest` run.

Key observations so far:
- Root pyproject has `testpaths = ["apps", "packages", "tests", "website"]` — `brand/tests` is NOT in testpaths! That's a significant issue for the design doc's claim that "the new `brand/tests` must pass under the root `uv run pytest` run." Unless the brand tests live under one of those paths, or testpaths gets updated. Actually wait — `brand/tests` would not be collected by `uv run pytest` at root since testpaths is set. That's a real question: does `brand/tests/test_brand_assets.py` get collected? It would need testpaths to include "brand" or the test file to be placed elsewhere. This is a plan-affecting detail.
- `pythonpath = ["."]` — so `brand/src/odi_mascot.py` would be importable as `brand.src.odi_mascot`? Only if `brand` and `brand/src` are packages (with `__init__.py`) or namespace packages. Python 3.3+ namespace packages would allow `import brand.src.odi_mascot` if root is on sys.path. Hmm, but `brand/src` as a namespace package... `import brand.src.odi_mascot` would work via implicit namespace packages since `brand` has no `__init__.py`. Actually yes, Python 3.3+ supports implicit namespace packages, so `brand.src.odi_mascot` is importable when cwd (root) is on sys.path. But `src` as a package name is odd. The question: how is the generator module imported by the tests and the render tool? `uv run python brand/tools/render.py` — running a script directly puts `brand/tools` on sys.path, not the repo root, so `from brand.src.odi_mascot import ...` would fail unless sys.path manipulation or `uv run python -m brand.tools.render`. That's a real implementation question. Let me check the existing repo's `scripts/` dir for conventions.
- `pytest-cov` `source` list doesn't include brand — coverage may fail if coverage requires all source covered? `source` just sets what's measured; not a hard failure.
- ruff: `extend-exclude` includes `.worktrees`... wait, that's relative to the root. The worktree root is /home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/.worktrees/odi-mascot, so when running ruff there, the paths are relative to that root, so `.worktrees` won't match. Fine.
- root ruff line-length 100, target py310.

Now let me look at the studio app files, CLI files, CI workflow, README.

display.text:
"""Guard against importing heavy dependencies at CLI module load time.

``agentic-odi --version`` and ``--help`` must not pull in the MCP client,
the connectors package, or the core domain layer just to run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys

_HEAVY_MODULES = ("fastmcp", "agentic_odi_connectors", "agentic_odi_core", "openai")


def test_importing_cli_entrypoint_does_not_load_heavy_modules():
    code = (
        "import sys; import agentic_odi_cli.cli; "
        "print(','.join(m for m in "
        f"{list(_HEAVY_MODULES)!r} if m in sys.modules))"
    )
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    loaded = [name for name in result.stdout.strip().split(",") if name]
    assert loaded == [], f"heavy modules imported at load time: {loaded}"

metadata.preview:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

display.text:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$SIGNING_KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build
          else
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

<content>
1: """Interactive conversational mode for the Agentic ODI CLI.
2: 
3: The chat is a small terminal REPL around an OpenAI-compatible model and the
4: Agentic ODI MCP server. It streams assistant text, executes MCP tool calls,
5: and keeps the conversation history in memory for the duration of the session.
6: """
7: 
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import asyncio
11: import json
12: import os
13: import traceback
14: from collections.abc import Callable
15: from dataclasses import dataclass
16: from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol
17: 
18: import typer
19: from agentic_odi_core import ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
20: from fastmcp import Client
21: from openai import AsyncOpenAI
22: 
23: DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
24: DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
25: DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
26: DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"
27: 
28: SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
29:     ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
30:     + """
31: 
32: You are running in a terminal chat. Use the available MCP tools to create and
33: query Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes instead of inventing
34: records or IDs. Follow the ODI outcome statement format and flag opportunity
35: scores above 10 as underserved. Keep answers concise and readable as plain text.
36: """
37: )
38: 
39: HELP_TEXT = """Commands:
40:   /help      Show this help
41:   /status    Show connection status (model, MCP server)
42:   /connect   Configure LLM provider and MCP server (wizard)
43:   /model <name>  Switch to a different model
44:   /mcp <url>     Reconnect to a different MCP server
45:   /clear     Clear the conversation history
46:   /tools     List the MCP tools available to the assistant
47:   /exit      Quit (also /quit)
48: 
49: Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""
50: 
51: 
52: @dataclass(frozen=True)
53: class ChatConfig:
54:     """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""
55: 
56:     base_url: str
57:     api_key: str
58:     model: str
59:     mcp_url: str
60: 
61:     @classmethod
62:     def from_env(
63:         cls,
64:         *,
65:         base_url: str | None = None,
66:         api_key: str | None = None,
67:         model: str | None = None,
68:         mcp_url: str | None = None,
69:     ) -> ChatConfig:
70:         """Resolve settings in priority order: explicit arg > env var > LLM profile > default."""
71:         # Lazy import to avoid circular imports between chat and profile.
72:         from agentic_odi_cli.profile import load_llm_profile  # noqa: PLC0415
73: 
74:         try:
75:             llm_profile = load_llm_profile()
76:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
77:             llm_profile = None
78: 
79:         return cls(
80:             base_url=(
81:                 base_url
82:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
83:                 or (llm_profile.base_url if llm_profile else None)
84:                 or DEFAULT_BASE_URL
85:             ),
86:             api_key=(
87:                 api_key
88:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY")
89:                 or (llm_profile.api_key if llm_profile else None)
90:                 or DEFAULT_API_KEY
91:             ),
92:             model=(
93:                 model
94:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL")
95:                 or (llm_profile.model if llm_profile else None)
96:                 or DEFAULT_MODEL
97:             ),
98:             mcp_url=(
99:                 mcp_url
100:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL")
101:                 or (llm_profile.mcp_url if llm_profile else None)
102:                 or DEFAULT_MCP_URL
103:             ),
104:         )
105: 
106: 
107: @dataclass
108: class ConnectionState:
109:     """Mutable connection status for a chat session."""
110: 
111:     llm_ok: bool = False
112:     mcp_ok: bool = False
113:     mcp_tool_count: int = 0
114:     error_llm: str | None = None
115:     error_mcp: str | None = None
116: 
117: 
118: class ChatSessionLike(Protocol):
119:     """The session surface the command handler needs."""
120: 
121:     tool_names: list[str]
122:     config: ChatConfig
123:     connection_state: ConnectionState
124: 
125:     def clear(self) -> None: ...
126: 
127:     def update_config(self, config: ChatConfig) -> None: ...
128: 
129: 
130: def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
131:     """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
132:     return [
133:         {
134:             "type": "function",
135:             "function": {
136:                 "name": tool.name,
137:                 "description": tool.description or "",
138:                 "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
139:             },
140:         }
141:         for tool in tools
142:     ]
143: 
144: 
145: def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
146:     """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
147:     return [
148:         {
149:             "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
150:             "type": "function",
151:             "function": {
152:                 "name": entry["name"],
153:                 "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
154:             },
155:         }
156:         for index, entry in entries.items()
157:     ]
158: 
159: 
160: def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
161:     """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
162:     content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
163:     parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
164:     text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
165:     return text or str(result)
166: 
167: 
168: def handle_command(
169:     line: str,
170:     session: ChatSessionLike,
171:     *,
172:     on_connect: Callable[[], ChatConfig | None] | None = None,
173:     on_mcp_reconnect: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None,
174: ) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | tuple[str, str] | None:
175:     """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message.
176: 
177:     Returns:
178:         "exit"              — caller should end the session.
179:         "handled"           — command was handled; continue the REPL.
180:         ("reconnect_mcp", url) — caller should reconnect MCP then continue.
181:         None                — not a command; caller should send to the LLM.
182:     """
183:     command = line.strip().lower()
184:     if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
185:         return "exit"
186:     if command == "/help":
187:         typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
188:         return "handled"
189:     if command == "/clear":
190:         session.clear()
191:         typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
192:         return "handled"
193:     if command == "/tools":
194:         if session.tool_names:
195:             typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
196:         else:
197:             typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
198:         return "handled"
199:     if command == "/status":
200:         state = session.connection_state
201:         llm_status = "connected" if state.llm_ok else "not connected"
202:         mcp_status = (
203:             f"connected ({state.mcp_tool_count} tools)" if state.mcp_ok else "not connected"
204:         )
205:         typer.echo(f"model  : {session.config.model}  [{llm_status}]")
206:         typer.echo(f"url    : {session.config.base_url}")
207:         typer.echo(f"mcp    : {session.config.mcp_url}  [{mcp_status}]")
208:         return "handled"
209:     if command.startswith("/model"):
210:         parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
211:         if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
212:             typer.echo(f"Current model: {session.config.model}")
213:         else:
214:             new_model = parts[1].strip()
215:             new_config = ChatConfig(
216:                 base_url=session.config.base_url,
217:                 api_key=session.config.api_key,
218:                 model=new_model,
219:                 mcp_url=session.config.mcp_url,
220:             )
221:             session.update_config(new_config)
222:             typer.echo(f"Model set to: {new_model}")
223:         return "handled"
224:     if command.startswith("/mcp"):
225:         parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
226:         if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
227:             typer.echo(f"Current MCP URL: {session.config.mcp_url}")
228:         else:

"""Interactive conversational mode for the Agentic ODI CLI.

The chat is a small terminal REPL around an OpenAI-compatible model and the
Agentic ODI MCP server. It streams assistant text, executes MCP tool calls,
and keeps the conversation history in memory for the duration of the session.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import traceback
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol

import typer
from agentic_odi_core import ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
from fastmcp import Client
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
    + """

You are running in a terminal chat. Use the available MCP tools to create and
query Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes instead of inventing
records or IDs. Follow the ODI outcome statement format and flag opportunity
scores above 10 as underserved. Keep answers concise and readable as plain text.
"""
)

HELP_TEXT = """Commands:
  /help      Show this help
  /status    Show connection status (model, MCP server)
  /connect   Configure LLM provider and MCP server (wizard)
  /model <name>  Switch to a different model
  /mcp <url>     Reconnect to a different MCP server
  /clear     Clear the conversation history
  /tools     List the MCP tools available to the assistant
  /exit      Quit (also /quit)

Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChatConfig:
    """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""

    base_url: str
    api_key: str
    model: str
    mcp_url: str

    @classmethod
    def from_env(
        cls,
        *,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        mcp_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> ChatConfig:
        """Resolve settings in priority order: explicit arg > env var > LLM profile > default."""
        # Lazy import to avoid circular imports between chat and profile.
        from agentic_odi_cli.profile import load_llm_profile  # noqa: PLC0415

        try:
            llm_profile = load_llm_profile()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            llm_profile = None

        return cls(
            base_url=(
                base_url
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
                or (llm_profile.base_url if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_BASE_URL
            ),
            api_key=(
                api_key
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY")
                or (llm_profile.api_key if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_API_KEY
            ),
            model=(
                model
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL")
                or (llm_profile.model if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_MODEL
            ),
            mcp_url=(
                mcp_url
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL")
                or (llm_profile.mcp_url if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_MCP_URL
            ),
        )


@dataclass
class ConnectionState:
    """Mutable connection status for a chat session."""

    llm_ok: bool = False
    mcp_ok: bool = False
    mcp_tool_count: int = 0
    error_llm: str | None = None
    error_mcp: str | None = None


class ChatSessionLike(Protocol):
    """The session surface the command handler needs."""

    tool_names: list[str]
    config: ChatConfig
    connection_state: ConnectionState

    def clear(self) -> None: ...

    def update_config(self, config: ChatConfig) -> None: ...


def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
    return [
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": tool.name,
                "description": tool.description or "",
                "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
            },
        }
        for tool in tools
    ]


def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
    return [
        {
            "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": entry["name"],
                "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
            },
        }
        for index, entry in entries.items()
    ]


def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
    """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
    content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
    parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
    text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
    return text or str(result)


def handle_command(
    line: str,
    session: ChatSessionLike,
    *,
    on_connect: Callable[[], ChatConfig | None] | None = None,
    on_mcp_reconnect: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None,
) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | tuple[str, str] | None:
    """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message.

    Returns:
        "exit"              — caller should end the session.
        "handled"           — command was handled; continue the REPL.
        ("reconnect_mcp", url) — caller should reconnect MCP then continue.
        None                — not a command; caller should send to the LLM.
    """
    command = line.strip().lower()
    if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
        return "exit"
    if command == "/help":
        typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
        return "handled"
    if command == "/clear":
        session.clear()
        typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/tools":
        if session.tool_names:
            typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
        else:
            typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/status":
        state = session.connection_state
        llm_status = "connected" if state.llm_ok else "not connected"
        mcp_status = (
            f"connected ({state.mcp_tool_count} tools)" if state.mcp_ok else "not connected"
        )
        typer.echo(f"model  : {session.config.model}  [{llm_status}]")
        typer.echo(f"url    : {session.config.base_url}")
        typer.echo(f"mcp    : {session.config.mcp_url}  [{mcp_status}]")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/model"):
        parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
        if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
            typer.echo(f"Current model: {session.config.model}")
        else:
            new_model = parts[1].strip()
            new_config = ChatConfig(
                base_url=session.config.base_url,
                api_key=session.config.api_key,
                model=new_model,
                mcp_url=session.config.mcp_url,
            )
            session.update_config(new_config)
            typer.echo(f"Model set to: {new_model}")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/mcp"):
        parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
        if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
            typer.echo(f"Current MCP URL: {session.config.mcp_url}")
        else:
            new_url = parts[1].strip()
            if on_mcp_reconnect is not None:
                ok = on_mcp_reconnect(new_url)
                if ok:
                    typer.echo(
                        f"MCP reconnected: {new_url} ({session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count} tools)"
                    )
                else:
                    typer.echo(f"Failed to connect to MCP at {new_url}")
            else:
                typer.echo("MCP reconnect not available in this context.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/connect":
        if on_connect is not None:
            connected_config = on_connect()
            if connected_config is not None:
                typer.echo(f"Connected: {connected_config.model} @ {connected_config.base_url}")
        else:
            typer.echo("Connect wizard not available in this context.")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/"):
        typer.echo(f"Unknown command: {line}. Type /help for commands.")
        return "handled"
    return None


async def _try_connect_mcp(mcp_url: str) -> tuple[Any, list[Any], str | None]:
    """Attempt to connect to the MCP server and list its tools.

    Returns:
        (mcp_client, tools, None) on success.
        (None, [], error_message) on failure.
    """
    try:
        async with Client(mcp_url) as c:
            tools = await c.list_tools()
        # Re-create a fresh context manager for the caller to manage lifetime.
        return Client(mcp_url), tools, None
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return None, [], str(exc)


class ChatSession:
    """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: ChatConfig,
        openai_client: Any,
        mcp_client: Any,
        *,
        connection_state: ConnectionState | None = None,
        on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,

        self.openai_client = openai_client

            connection_state if connection_state is not None else ConnectionState()
        )

        self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
        self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.tool_names: list[str] = []

        """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
        tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
        self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
        self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]

    def update_config(self, new_config: ChatConfig) -> None:
        """Hot-swap the session config and mark the LLM connection as live."""
        self.config = new_config
        self.connection_state.llm_ok = True

    async def _stream_completion(
        self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
    ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
        stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self.config.model,
            messages=self.messages,
            tools=self.tools or None,
            tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
            stream=True,
        )

        content_parts: list[str] = []
        tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}

                content_parts.append(content)
                if on_delta is not None:

                entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
                    tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
                )
                if tool_call.id:
                    entry["id"] = tool_call.id
                function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)
                if function is not None:
                    if function.name:
                        entry["name"] = function.name
                    if function.arguments:
                        entry["arguments"] += function.arguments

        return "".join(content_parts), tool_calls

    async def _call_tool(self, call: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        name = call["function"]["name"]
        raw_arguments = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
        try:
            arguments = json.loads(raw_arguments)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return f"Error: invalid JSON arguments for {name}: {raw_arguments}"
        if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
            return f"Error: arguments for {name} must be a JSON object"
        if self.on_tool is not None:
            self.on_tool(name, arguments)
        try:
            result = await self.mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
        return _tool_result_text(result)

    async def ask(self, text: str, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> str:
        """Send a message, execute any tool calls, and return the final text."""
        if not self.connection_state.llm_ok:
            return "No model connected. Type /connect to set one up."

        checkpoint = len(self.messages)
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
        try:
            while True:
                content, tool_calls = await self._stream_completion(on_delta)
                if not tool_calls:
                    self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
                    return content

                normalized = _normalize_tool_calls(tool_calls)
                self.messages.append(
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": content or None, "tool_calls": normalized}
                )
                for call in normalized:
                    result = await self._call_tool(call)
                    self.messages.append(
                        {
                            "role": "tool",
                            "tool_call_id": call["id"],
                            "name": call["function"]["name"],
                            "content": result,
                        }
                    )
        except Exception:
            del self.messages[checkpoint:]
            raise


def _print_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    rendered = json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
    if len(rendered) > 100:
        rendered = rendered[:97] + "..."
    typer.secho(f"  → {name} {rendered}", fg="bright_black", err=True)


async def _run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> int:
    typer.echo("Agentic ODI · interactive")

    llm: Any | None = None
    conn = ConnectionState()

    try:
        # --- MCP connection (optional) ---
        mcp_client_ctx, tools, mcp_error = await _try_connect_mcp(config.mcp_url)
        if mcp_error is None:
            conn.mcp_ok = True
            conn.mcp_tool_count = len(tools)
        else:
            conn.error_mcp = mcp_error
            typer.secho(
                f"⚠  MCP unavailable ({config.mcp_url}): {mcp_error}",
                fg="yellow",
                err=False,
            )
            typer.secho(
                "   Starting without MCP tools. Use /mcp to reconnect.",
                fg="yellow",
                err=False,
            )

        # --- LLM client (always created; actual reachability found on first use) ---
        llm = AsyncOpenAI(
            base_url=config.base_url,
            api_key=config.api_key,
            timeout=60.0,
        )
        conn.llm_ok = True

        # --- Startup banner ---
        mcp_status = f"✓ {conn.mcp_tool_count} tools" if conn.mcp_ok else "✗ offline"
        typer.echo(f"model: {config.model}  ·  mcp: {config.mcp_url} [{mcp_status}]")
        typer.echo("Type /help for commands, /exit to quit.\n")

        # --- Build session ---
        session = ChatSession(
            config,
            llm,
            mcp_client_ctx,  # may be None if MCP is offline
            connection_state=conn,
            on_tool=_print_tool,
        )

        # Populate tools from the probe we already did (avoids a second round-trip).
        if conn.mcp_ok and tools:
            session.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
            session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]

        # --- REPL ---
        while True:
            try:
                line = input("you › ").strip()
            except EOFError:
                typer.echo()
                break
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                typer.echo("\nUse /exit to quit.")
                continue

            if not line:
                continue

            def _on_connect() -> ChatConfig | None:
                from agentic_odi_cli.wizard import run_connect_wizard  # noqa: PLC0415

                new_config = run_connect_wizard(session.config)
                if new_config is not None:
                    session.update_config(new_config)
                return new_config

            def _on_mcp_reconnect(new_url: str) -> bool:
                """Run MCP reconnect in a separate thread (avoids nested event loops)."""
                import concurrent.futures  # noqa: PLC0415

                async def _reconnect() -> bool:
                    _, new_tools, err = await _try_connect_mcp(new_url)
                    if err is not None:
                        return False
                    new_config = ChatConfig(
                        base_url=session.config.base_url,
                        api_key=session.config.api_key,
                        model=session.config.model,
                        mcp_url=new_url,
                    )
                    session.update_config(new_config)
                    session.mcp_client = Client(new_url)
                    session.tools = _to_openai_tools(new_tools)
                    session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]
                    session.connection_state.mcp_ok = True
                    session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count = len(new_tools)
                    return True

                with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
                    future = executor.submit(asyncio.run, _reconnect())
                    return future.result()

            action = handle_command(
                line, session, on_connect=_on_connect, on_mcp_reconnect=_on_mcp_reconnect
            )
            if action == "exit":
                break
            if action == "handled":
                continue

            typer.secho("odi › ", fg="green", bold=True, nl=False)
            printed = False

            def on_delta(piece: str) -> None:
                nonlocal printed
                printed = True
                typer.echo(piece, nl=False)

            try:
                reply = await session.ask(line, on_delta=on_delta)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                typer.echo()
                typer.echo(f"Error: {exc}", err=True)
                if os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DEBUG"):
                    typer.echo(traceback.format_exc(), err=True)
                continue
            typer.echo()
            if not printed:
                typer.echo(reply if reply else "(no response)")

    finally:
        if llm is not None:
            await llm.close()

    typer.echo("Goodbye.")
    return 0


def run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> None:
    """Run the interactive chat until the user exits."""
    try:
        exit_code = asyncio.run(_run_chat(config))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        typer.echo("\nGoodbye.")
        return
    if exit_code:
        raise typer.Exit(code=exit_code)

# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the static page lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)** and is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, and the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity boards, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** hands a new user off to the context conversation or straight to a surface. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio it asks — conversationally, in the chat, and skippable at any point — for your product, audience, and the job your customers are trying to get done. Answer what you like; every reply starts from what you shared. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## License This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ---
